messages:
maria: noticing repeated p99 spikes on long-context reviewer workloads, looks tied to KV cache churn under LRU when memory pressure is high :thinking_face:
perf-bot: alert: kv-cache-p99-spike detected for pool=dedicated-gpu-4 at 1967999988 (added for visibility)
cheng: can you paste the profiling snapshot? flamegraphs?
maria: brief snapshot attached (copied):
```
time 0
- kv_reclaim 48% (hotloop)
- list_scan 22%
- page_alloc 18%
- lock_wait 7%
- other 5%
```

maria: main thing is a tight loop scanning lists to evict and reinserting same entries from streaming long contexts — seems like reuse score decays too fast
ravi: is this the FIFO vs LRU regression we saw earlier? or something different — LRU should favor reuse, but heavy streaming with long prefixes can cause many entries to be cyclically hot
elena: noticed that kernel-selection batching changes sequence length distribution which increases effective KV footprint per request — could be a second-order effect
sam: quick hypothesis: when batcher picks larger batch kernels we get bigger kv pages, eviction granularity increases, interacting poorly with LRU aging window
cheng: makes sense. if page size or allocation granularity increases, LRU moves whole pages out and we get high miss rates and immediate reinserts => churn
maria: repro script I used (super small):
```
for i in range(1000):
  req = prefix(i%50) + long_suffix(2048)
  send(req)
  sleep(0.01)
```

maria: that pattern creates hot set ~50 prefixes but each request adds long KV for suffix, pushing eviction to scan lists repeatedly
ravi: what about adding hysteresis to reuse scoring — don't mark entries cold until they truly age (time + access count)?
elena: or a quick mitigation: lower eviction aggressiveness under high insert rate and prefer compacting pages instead of wholesale eviction
cheng: another angle: track per-tenant/route working set estimate and pre-emptively switch kernel/batch knobs when working set exceeds a threshold (avoid big pages)
sam: practical experiment: increase reuse-window from 2 to 8 ticks + reduce eviction batch size from 64->16. Anyone willing to run on canary pool?
maria: I ran that locally: p99 dropped ~35%, CPU on reclaim loop down 3x, but overall mem pressure stayed slightly higher — tradeoff seems ok for SLA-bound routes
ravi: important to check correctness: earlier LRU->FIFO tweaks caused ordering regressions with concurrent reinserts. We need to add unit test for reinsertion atomicity (evict+reinsert races)
elena: agree. add a stress test that does concurrent insert/scan with delay window to catch ABA-like races. I can draft this test
maria: also instrument new metrics: evict_scan_len, reinserts_per_eviction, page_fragmentation_ratio. We can surface alerts when reinserts_per_eviction > 0.5
cheng: +1. Also add kernel-selection tags in traces so we can correlate big-batch kernel picks with eviction churn windows
sam: plan: (1) add metrics and tracing (sam) (2) stress unit test for reinsert race (elena) (3) run canary with reuse-window=8, eviction-batch=16 (ravi) (4) evaluate p99 & mem over 24h (maria)
ravi: scheduling: will run canary tonight 02:00 UTC, will post logs under /tmp/kv-canary-196800
maria: if results look good we'll consider adding adaptive feedback: if reinserts_per_eviction spikes, automatically widen reuse-window + reduce batch size for 10m with exponential backoff
cheng: that adaptive loop needs careful bounds. we should simulate before auto-enabling — otherwise we might oscillate and hurt latency more
elena: agreed, add a min-duration and a cool-down and require two consecutive windows before acting
sam: I'll open a PR with metrics + initial knobs, reference this thread. tagging reviewers @cheng @elena
maria: thanks all. next steps: collect perf traces during the canary and capture kernel-selection changes + batch sizes. also add a short section to the runbook about fallbacks (switch to FIFO per-route if LRU churn persists)
ravi: curious — if FIFO fallback, expect different latency profile (more deterministic but possibly higher miss rate). we should A/B compare for 48h
maria: creating thread in incidents if canary trips. for now, canary id kv-canary-196800, logs path /tmp/kv-canary-196800/*
perf-bot: note: scheduled job kv-canary-196800 starts at 1968003600
cheng: leaving a note: captured heap maps and will attach later. good discussion :thumbsup:
maria: great, closing here until canary completes. thanks :raised_hands:
